accepted.question_text: Let f be a multiplicative arithmetic function with property P, meaning that f(p^alpha) depends only on the exponent alpha and not on the prime p. Suppose f(p^alpha) grows like the divisor function value alpha + 1, but the ratio log f(p^2) / log f(p) is a Liouville number. If Q_f(X) denotes the number of f-champion numbers N <= X, where an integer N is f-champion when every M < N has f(M) < f(N), must there exist a constant c_f such that Q_f(X) = O((log X)^c_f) as X grows?

accepted.question_text: For multiplicative arithmetic functions f with property P, where f(p^alpha) depends only on alpha, every f-champion number lies in the set W of positive integers whose prime-exponent sequence is nonincreasing: if p and q divide N and p < q, then v_p(N) >= v_q(N). Since the counting function W(X) is therefore a universal upper bound for Q_f(X), can one find a smaller universal upper bound for Q_f(X) that is valid for every such f?

accepted.question_text: Study the hyper abundant numbers: integers N for which there is a real parameter u such that, for every integer M >= 1, sigma(M) / (M (log M)^u) <= sigma(N) / (N (log N)^u), where sigma(n) is the sum of divisors of n. Can the methods used by Guy Robin for hyper composite numbers be adapted to obtain structural or counting results for these hyper abundant numbers?

evidence.quote: Probably, the method used by G. Robin in [39] can be adapted to study hyper abundant numbers
but, as far as I know, nobody did it.

accepted.question_text: Let 1 = d_1 < d_2 < ... < d_tau(n) = n be the increasing sequence of positive divisors of n, and define H(n) as the sum of 1 / (d_j - d_i) over all pairs 1 <= i < j <= tau(n). Is H(n) < tau(n) for every n > 5040, equivalently for every n outside the listed exceptional set {12, 24, 60, 120, 180, 240, 360, 420, 720, 840, 1260, 1680, 2520, 5040}?

evidence.quote: Does H(n) < tau (n) hold for n > 5040?
It is conjectured in [11] (cf. also [25], problem 23, p. 200)

accepted.question_text: For H(n) defined from the divisor sequence of n by summing 1 / (d_j - d_i) over all pairs of distinct divisors d_i < d_j, are there only finitely many exceptions to the inequality H(n) < tau(n)?

evidence.quote: the question are there finitely many exceptions to the inequality H(n) < tau (n) remains open.

accepted.question_text: For the same divisor-gap harmonic sum H(n), prove or disprove that the maximum value of H(n) / tau(n) over positive integers n is attained at n = 60 and equals H(60) / tau(60), approximately 1.126.

evidence.quote: Another open question is to show that max H(n) > tau(n) = H(60)
